findings.description: READ-ONLY IS STATED BY THE SPEC AND PINNED NOWHERE IN CODE. SHEET-TAB-001 says "publish four read-only view tabs". All three A-runs implement it (A1 `ViewTab.protected: bool` = true for all four; A2 assumption 9 "protected ranges, no user-editable cells... applied by the publisher"; A3 `protected: true` consumed by the publisher). The real code has no such concept anywhere: `sheets_view::ViewTab` is `{ name, header, rows }` with no protection field; the `SheetsViewClient` trait's entire surface is `batch_update_view` / `set_tab_order` / `read_price_pass` / `write_stale_banner` — no protected-range or `addProtectedRange` operation; `ViewSheetsAdapter` issues only `update_range` and `ensure_sheet`; no test in tabs.rs or cold_start.rs asserts protection. The code in fact assumes the opposite — tabs.rs `republish_regenerates_data_and_never_rewrites_frozen_header` comments "a human-inserted/sorted row is overwritten by design", i.e. the tabs are user-writable and republish simply clobbers. The word "read-only" in the EARS buys nothing.

THE SPEC SAYS FOUR TABS; THE CODE EMITS A FIFTH NAMED BAND. A-side closes the set at four by construction (A1/A2/A3 all use a 4-variant `TabKind` with `ALL: [TabKind; 4]`). B-side unanimously reconstructs a fifth: `TAX_RESERVE_TAB = "Tax · Reserve Summary"` with its own 7-column `TAX_RESERVE_HEADER` (Jurisdiction, Tax Year, Accrued, Moved, Paid, Outstanding, Shortfall) — and all three B-runs feel compelled to add the disclaimer "not a fifth view tab", which is exactly the tell that the spec text does not cover it. In code it is a full `ViewTab` with a tab-shaped `name`, so `ViewSheetsAdapter::batch_update_view` would write `'Tax · Reserve Summary'!A2:Z` and `ensure_sheet` it into existence — a real fifth Sheets tab that `workbook_tab_order()` (10 entries, TAX_RESERVE_TAB absent) then never positions. The EARS states neither the band nor its exemption from the count of four.

THE EXACT PER-TAB COLUMN SCHEMAS ARE CODE-ONLY. The spec says only "typed headers"; the code pins five frozen header constants, and all three B-runs recovered them character-for-character: POSITIONS_HEADER 13 cols A–M (Symbol, Shares, Avg Cost/Share, Total Basis, Price, Market Value, Unrealized P&L, Est. Tax Rate, Est. Unrealized Tax (est), Net Unrealized (est), Unrealized %, Realized P&L, Quote Date); OPEN_LOTS_HEADER 10; REALIZED_HEADER 11; TAX_HEADER 6; TAX_RESERVE_HEADER 7. Column count and order are load-bearing (see the read-back indices finding) yet nothing in the EARS constrains them.

THE MARKS READ-BACK IS POSITIONALLY COUPLED TO THE BAND SHAPE BY HARD-CODED INDEX, UNSTATED. runtime/src/adapters.rs `price_reading_from_cells` pins `const PRICE_COL: usize = 4` and `const QUOTE_DATE_COL: usize = 12`; `read_price_pass` keys row identity on `cells.first()` (Symbol, column 0) and silently `continue`s on any row whose first cell is empty. All three B-runs state these indices. The EARS's "one row per entity with typed headers" is what makes this safe, but the spec never says the price oracle column is index 4, the quote-date companion index 12, or that identity is column 0 — so any header reordering silently re-points the live-price settle pass at the wrong column with no test tripping.

THE FULL 10-TAB WORKBOOK ORDER AND ITS IDEMPOTENT REASSERT ARE CODE-ONLY. `workbook_tab_order()` pins Positions, Open Lots, Realized, Tax, History, Tax Rules, Residency, Platforms & Aliases, Ledger Events, Tax Events — Positions leftmost (landing), event logs the final two — reasserted on every `Publisher::republish` (tabs.rs `republish_idempotently_reasserts_tab_order` asserts two republishes yield identical order), and a failed `set_tab_order` flips `RepublishOutcome.published` to false. The EARS names four tabs and says nothing about ordering, about the six non-view tabs, about Positions being the landing tab, or about sheets-view owning the placement of tabs other segments own.

"TYPED HEADERS" IS UNDERSPECIFIED AND THE CODE'S ACTUAL TYPING RULE IS UNSTATED. A-side: the spec says "typed" but not what typing means, so all three A-runs invented a column type system (A1 `ColType`, A2 `CellType` + a hard `TabError::CellType` on any data cell whose type disagrees with its header, A3 `ColType` with Percent). Real code carries no type at all: `header: Vec<String>`, and cells are `Cell::Value(String)` / `Cell::Formula(String)` — the only distinction is engine-value vs live formula, everything is a string, and tabs.rs asserts nothing stronger than `assert!(!positions.header.is_empty())`. B-side: the code's real typing mechanism is delegation to Sheets — the `batch_update_view` contract requires `USER_ENTERED` so `"20.0000%"` (from `fmt_ppm`) coerces to numeric 0.20 for `=G*H` / `=G*(1-H)` to multiply, and `runtime::sheets` pins `valueInputOption=USER_ENTERED` on `update_range` while event rows ride RAW. Neither the type-declaration reading nor the coercion rule appears in the EARS.

THE PURPOSE CLAUSE — "SO NATIVE SHEETS FILTERING AND SORTING WORK DIRECTLY" — IS NOT PINNED, AND REPUBLISH ACTIVELY DEFEATS SORTING. A1/A3 both infer a frozen row 1 / filter-view setup from this clause (A1 assumption 12 "freeze-row/filter-view setup is the writer's job"; A3 assumption 4 "one header row, row 1, frozen (implied by 'filtering and sorting work directly')"). The code never configures either: no `frozenRowCount`, no `setBasicFilter` request exists in `SheetsViewClient`, `ViewSheetsAdapter`, or `GoogleSheetsApi` (whose batchUpdate use is limited to addSheet/deleteSheet). "Frozen header" in this codebase means only a write discipline — row 1 is written once at bootstrap and never rewritten. Worse, the atomic full-range rewrite discards any native sort the user applies (tabs.rs: "a human-inserted/sorted row is overwritten by design"), so the affordance the spec names as the requirement's whole justification survives only until the next sync.

PUBLISH-FAILURE SEMANTICS ARE ENTIRELY CODE-ONLY. `ViewError::{PublishFailed, SettleTimeout, DuplicateSymbolRow}`; `Publisher` owns a per-tab stale `BTreeSet`; on a failed `batch_update_view` it flags the tab stale, best-effort writes the literal banner `format!("STALE — last sync {stale_banner_quote_ts}")` to `'<tab>'!AA1` (the adapter's fixed anchor), leaves the tab as-is, sets `published: false`, and retries next sync. All three B-runs recovered this including the banner string and the AA1 cell. SHEET-TAB-001 states nothing about what happens when a publish fails, so nothing prevents a future change from making a failed tab silently disappear rather than go stale.

THE ROW ANCHOR AND REWRITE DISCIPLINE ARE CODE-ONLY CONSTANTS. `DATA_START_ROW: u32 = 2` (public const), data range `'<tab>'!A{DATA_START_ROW}:Z` (hard-capped at column Z), header written exactly once at `'<tab>'!A1` and never rewritten on republish, and the whole data range rewritten as ONE `update_range` with tail truncation to the exact row count. All three B-runs pin row 2, the A2:Z range, and the never-rewritten header; tabs.rs `republish_regenerates_data_and_never_rewrites_frozen_header` asserts `p2.header == p1.header` and `p2.rows.len() == 1` after shrinking from 2 rows. The EARS mentions no anchor row, no column bound, and no atomicity/truncation guarantee.

ONE-ROW-PER-ENTITY IS PROMOTED TO A LOUD REJECTION FOR ONE TAB ONLY. `render_positions` maintains a `seen: BTreeSet<&Symbol>` and returns `Err(ViewError::DuplicateSymbolRow(symbol))` on a repeat — a defensive guard the code itself documents as "structurally UNREACHABLE through the real API" because `Snapshot.positions` is a Map. All three B-runs surfaced it as a requirement. The spec's "one row per entity" is a shape statement with no error semantics, and the other three bands (`render_open_lots`, `render_realized`, `render_tax`) are infallible — they return `ViewTab`/`TaxView`, not `Result` — so the enforced-vs-assumed asymmetry is invisible from the EARS.

FRESH-WORKBOOK COLD START IS CODE-ONLY. `is_missing_tab` classifies the Sheets 400 whose message contains `"Unable to parse range"`; `batch_update_view` then calls `ensure_sheet`, writes the header once to `'<tab>'!A1`, and retries the data write (cold_start.rs `republish_to_a_fresh_workbook_creates_the_view_tab_with_its_frozen_header`), while `read_price_pass` treats a missing Positions tab as an EMPTY pass rather than an error (`the_price_pass_on_a_fresh_workbook_is_empty_not_an_error`). B1 and B2 both state the create-then-retry rule. SHEET-TAB-001 says "publish" and leaves whether publishing implies creating entirely open.

THE VIEW LAYER DOES ARITHMETIC THE SPEC'S SCOPE DISCLAIMS. sheets-view is framed as owning no accounting or tax math, yet `render_positions` computes Avg Cost/Share via `pt_core::round_half_to_even(total_basis × 1e6, total_qty)` (with a zero-shares guard yielding "0.00"), `render_open_lots` does the same for Basis/Share and classifies LT/ST via `tax::classify_term`, `render_realized` derives Term and `tax::tax_year_of` and defaults a missing lifecycle State to the literal "Accrued", and the Positions tab pushes post-tax estimate math into sheet formulas (`=G*H`, `=G*(1-H)`, `=IF(D=0,0,G/D)`). B3 enumerates the full formula set including the days-since-1970 quote-date encoding `=IFERROR(TEXT(INT(GOOGLEFINANCE(t,"tradetime"))-DATE(1970,1,1),"0"),"")`. None of this derived-column math is sanctioned or bounded by the EARS.

notes:
Classification rationale: both directions carry material surplus AND they collide on the same two underspecified phrases in SHEET-TAB-001 — \"four ... tabs\" (A closes the set at 4; B recovers a fifth named band the code needs a disclaimer to explain away) and \"typed headers\" (A invents a column type system the spec forces but does not define; B recovers the code's real, unstated typing rule — USER_ENTERED coercion of formatted strings). That overlap is what makes this BD-DRIFT rather than B-ONLY-DRIFT, even though B carries the larger raw volume.

A-side stability (high): all three runs independently produced a closed 4-variant TabKind with `ALL: [_; 4]`, the exact titles with \"Open Lots\" spaced, a per-column type carried beside the header, a `protected`/read-only flag delegated to the writer, empty-band-still-published, no imposed sort, and a Formula cell variant for GOOGLEFINANCE. They diverge only on two sub-decisions the spec genuinely leaves open: ragged-row handling (A1/A3 pad-and-truncate, A2 hard-errors with `TabError::Arity`) and whether a summary block above the header row is legal (A3 explicitly permits, A1 assumption 6 explicitly rejects). Neither divergence touches the findings.

B-side stability (high): B1/B2/B3 agree on every constant — the five header lists, the 10-tab order, DATA_START_ROW=2, A2:Z, col indices 0/4/12, DuplicateSymbolRow, the STALE banner at AA1, the cold-start create-then-retry, and the reserve-summary band. Near-identical reconstructions.

Assumption artifacts EXCLUDED as findings (unanimous A-side behavior with no basis in spec text): the fixed left-to-right publication order of the four tabs (the EARS enumerates but does not order them — I credited the ordering only on the B side, where the code pins it); `Cell::Blank` as a universal missing-value representation; row order delegated to the kernel; `&'static str` non-localized headers.

B-SIDE BLIND SPOTS worth flagging to the parent — code behavior none of the three B-runs reconstructed, so it is code-side surplus the differential did NOT surface: (1) `Publisher::republish` acquires an advisory `Lock` BEFORE any workbook mutation and, on `lock.acquire()` failure, writes NOTHING that cycle and returns `published: false` with the stale set unchanged — a non-destructive refusal all three B-runs missed; (2) `render_realized`'s silent `unwrap_or_else(|| \"Accrued\".to_string())` when no Federal accrual matches `(sale_id, lot_id)`, which mislabels a disposal's lifecycle State rather than blanking it; (3) `render_positions` renders an EMPTY `Est. Tax Rate` cell when a symbol is absent from `effective_rates`, which makes the post-tax formulas `=G*H` and `=G*(1-H)` silently degrade to 0 and to the pre-tax figure respectively.

One possible latent defect noticed while reading (not a differential finding, flagged for the arrow owner): `ViewSheetsAdapter::batch_update_view` passes an EMPTY grid to `update_range` when a band has zero rows. The in-memory fake truncates on update, but the real Sheets `values.update` with an empty `values` array writes nothing and does not clear the residual tail — so an entity band that empties out (all positions closed) may leave stale rows on the real workbook while every test passes.
